ceilings._token_definition: input_tokens + output_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens, summed across every fleet session in ~/.claude/projects/*Madhav*/ whose first message is at or after campaign_started_ts. Measured by bin/spend_meter.py into state/SPEND.jsonl. This is the raw four-class sum; it is dominated by cache_read (~97% of recent volume) and is therefore an AUDIT total, not a cost proxy and not a good runaway detector — see output_tokens_* for the tripwire that binds first in a loop.
ceilings._output_definition: output_tokens only, same sessions and window. Output is the best single proxy for work actually generated: cache_read scales with context size and session count, output scales with generation, so a fleet stuck in a loop trips this before the raw sum.
ceilings._cost_note: The ceiling that actually means money. NULL until state/PRICING.json carries current per-model, per-class rates — the four token classes differ by roughly an order of magnitude in price, so no single token count is a cost proxy. PRAHARI trips on whichever ceiling binds first; a null cost ceiling is simply not one of them yet.

open_threads.what: We were calling a working mechanism a defect. A TURN-BASED AGENT CANNOT SELF-LOOP PAST A TURN BOUNDARY: when PARIKSAKA finishes a batch its turn ends, and no instruction it gives itself can create its own next turn — only an incoming message or a scheduled trigger can. So 'always continue after each verdict' is a rule that cannot be followed, and issuing it would mean treating every violation as a lapse. PRAHARI's nudge IS the mechanism and is exactly what §18.6 puts in its hands: an agent idle with queued work is the anti-idle case. DISPOSITION: nudge on idle-with-non-empty-queue indefinitely; do NOT escalate it as a stall again. Worth flagging only if the SHAPE changes — the stuck-text mode returning, the queue growing while being nudged, or a nudge that produces no turn. EVIDENCE IT IS WORKING: the stuck-text mode is gone (a cleanly completed turn with an empty box is a different, benign state) and the queue went 38 -> 27 across one batch. The batch instruction did what it could — make each turn do more work — and could never have done more. IF drain rate ever becomes the binding constraint, the answer is a scheduled trigger for that session, which is a change to how the session is RUN and therefore the native's to make, not the fleet's.

fleet_addressing.note: Fleet agents are addressable by SESSION MESSAGE, not only by tmux keystrokes. standing_instructions.mutation_restore: REVISED after M0-T38 proved the earlier version insufficient. THE DEFECT IS THE SHAPE OF THE CHECK: 'sha256 == my-own-baseline' is a PROXY ('the file equals my copy') standing in for the CLAIM ('no mutation is present') — with a poisoned baseline it is structurally incapable of returning false. Our own §N.8 class, on the mechanism we use to trust our checks. R1 exclusivity — prefer a per-agent worktree when mutating; removes the class rather than detecting it. R2 PROVE THE BASELINE BEFORE MUTATING: its sha256 must equal the file's HEAD blob or a hash your own previous command printed; if neither, STOP — you have copied a sibling's in-flight state. IF ONLY ONE IS ADOPTED, ADOPT R2. R3 restore verification includes a MARKER SWEEP, not only baseline equality. R4 hash-bracket PRE/POST in one shell invocation for anything you will quote. R5 marker sweep immediately before committing. R6 delete the byte-copy. R7 (from M0-T43's near-miss against its own procedure): USE ABSOLUTE PATHS IN THE RESTORE. Its cp ran on a RELATIVE path after a cd earlier in the same compound command, SILENTLY FAILED, and left the file mutated until it read the output. Its conclusion is the sharp part and generalises to every mutation proof in this campaign: THE RESTORE IS THE ONE STEP WHOSE FAILURE THE MUTATION TEST CANNOT DETECT — the test is designed to fail while the mutation is present, so a failed restore looks exactly like a working test.

NEW DISPATCHES GO SHARED-TREE with strict R2 until the base-ref question is settled. R2 GAINS A SECOND CLAUSE, from M0-T41: prove your HEAD is the CAMPAIGN TIP, not merely that your file matches your HEAD — a file can match its HEAD perfectly and still be four hours stale.
standing_instructions.mutation_proof_doctrine: D-41, adopted verbatim as doctrine after the sentinel-on-failure finding (mutation C passed 6/6 because the throw happened outside the try its tests could reach): behavioural mutation testing is NECESSARY AND STRUCTURALLY INSUFFICIENT — it reaches only paths its author imagined, because the mutations and the tests are authored by the same mind and inherit the same assumptions about where the code can go. STANDING REQUIREMENT for every mutation proof from here: (1) pair behavioural testing with a STRUCTURAL assertion over the source (e.g. exactly one emission point, with paired positives so an empty result is not vacuous); (2) include at least one INVERSE-DIRECTION mutation — one that makes the signal fire when it should NOT, not only one that suppresses it; (3) state explicitly what the structural test does NOT establish. A proof whose limits are stated is worth more than a proof whose limits are assumed.
standing_instructions.ci_edit_classification: D-41: CI edits do NOT route through ADHIKARIN as a class — that would make it a bottleneck against a hazard that only runs one way. Classify by DIRECTION: could this change cause a build/deploy that previously FAILED to now PASS? STRENGTHENS (adds an assertion, removes continue-on-error, makes something fail that previously passed) = machinery, proceed and report, no ruling needed. WEAKENS (makes something pass that previously failed, disables or skips a check, adds continue-on-error, allowlists a failure, relaxes a threshold) = requires ADHIKARIN's ruling, presumptively H3. CANNOT TELL WHICH DIRECTION = treat as weakening. The catalogue-guards' blocking-switch constraint stays specific to that switch (flipping to blocking while criteria are non-zero creates H3 pressure) rather than generalising to every CI edit.
